answer: Make admission a scarce shared-liability berth, not a free name. A newcomer occupies a limited docking slot only when two incumbents who have not recently co-signed each other lock a joint bond against first-cycle fraud. Picture the desk at a river jetty: clerks will not release a pearl consignment until two independent skippers walk the barge in, and the cargo stays under a juniper warehouse seal until the newcomer settles a full cycle of counterparty work. Fake fleets stall because each extra identity consumes an unlinked signer pair and a berth they cannot recycle quickly.
